name: Stanley Black & Decker
fiscalYearEnd: 52/53-week year ending near December 31 (FY2025 ended January 3, 2026; EDGAR code 0102)

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Stanley Black & Decker Logo.svg)

description: Stanley Black & Decker is mostly a maker of power tools, hand tools, storage and outdoor equipment under DeWalt, Craftsman, Stanley, Black+Decker and Cub Cadet, which is 87 percent of its $15.1B 2025 revenue. A large share is sold through home centers and mass merchants (The Home Depot alone was about 15 percent of 2025 sales), the rest to professionals, distributors and dealers. The other 13 percent is Engineered Fastening: fasteners, rivets and other engineered components sold direct to automotive, electronics, construction and aerospace manufacturers. It has been shrinking to these two businesses through sales of Infrastructure (April 2024) and the Consolidated Aerospace Manufacturing business (April 6, 2026).

gics.note: Sector and sub-industry per Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies'; industry group and industry not given there. Mowgli note: 87 percent of revenue is consumer and pro tools and outdoor equipment sold mainly through home centers, so the industrial-machinery box misdescribes it.

employees.note: FY2025 10-K: about 43,500 employees in 59 countries (about 35% in the US), plus about 6,300 temporary contractors

businessLines.name: Tools & Outdoor
businessLines.how: One-time sale of tools and equipment, mostly to home centers, mass merchants and hardware stores plus distributors, dealers and a direct sales force; heavy on batteries and platforms that lock buyers into a brand's tool ecosystem; margin depends on tariffs, price and volume.
businessLines.description: Power Tools Group (professional DeWalt cordless and corded tools; Craftsman and Stanley for DIY; Black+Decker household products), Hand Tools, Accessories & Storage, and Outdoor Power Equipment (Cub Cadet, Hustler, electric and gas lawn and garden).

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 $1,197.4M (9.0%). Share is of segment total $1,525.8M (computed). Six months to 2026-07-04 $665.0M vs $527.3M; Q2 2026 includes a $118.0M IEEPA tariff-refund gain in cost of sales (partly offset by $83.4M of related costs, company-wide).

businessLines.name: Engineered Fastening
businessLines.how: Design-in sales of application-specific components and installation tools to manufacturers, mostly through a direct sales force; revenue follows customer production volume (notably automotive). The Consolidated Aerospace Manufacturing aerospace business was sold April 6, 2026.
businessLines.description: Fasteners, blind rivets and tools, blind inserts, drawn arc weld studs, self-piercing riveting systems, engineered plastic and mechanical fasteners, latches, heat shields and related components for automotive, manufacturing, electronics, construction and aerospace.

revenue.note: FY2024 $2,061.5M (-4%, including the April 2024 Infrastructure sale). Q2 2026 $396.4M; six months to 2026-07-04 profit $112.5M vs $74.0M.
